Adjacency between the features of a geoframe

Source: R/adjacent.R
geoscale_adjacent.Rd

Builds the neighbour matrix of a geoframe from attached geometry: which of its codes share a border with which. The result is what nestedscales::cluster_contiguous(adjacency =) consumes.

Usage

geoscale_adjacent(
  x,
  geoframe = NULL,
  within = NULL,
  contiguity = c("queen", "rook"),
  isolated = c("none", "nearest"),
  precision = 0
)

Arguments

x

A GeoScale with geometry attached (see attach_geometry_geoscale()).

geoframe

Geoframe whose features are compared. Defaults to the atom geoframe. Geometry is dissolved to it first, so any geoframe works.

within

Optional coarser geoframe whose boundaries cut edges: two features in different within codes are never neighbours. NULL (default) keeps every border. Use it to confine a clustering to a parent, which also sets the floor on the number of groups obtainable — a clustering cannot merge below the number of connected components.

contiguity

"queen" (default) counts contact of any dimension, so features meeting at a single corner are neighbours; "rook" requires a shared border of non-zero length. On a gridded or hexagonal lattice the two differ, and on real coastlines they occasionally do too, where three borders meet at a point.

isolated

What to do with a feature that borders nothing — an island, an exclave, or a feature cut off by within. "none" (default) leaves it isolated. "nearest" joins it to the closest other feature, which is what a clustering needs to avoid a group of one. A distance tolerance is deliberately not offered: one wide enough to bridge a strait also links every pair of cells one apart on a lattice.

precision

Optional GEOS precision passed to geoscale_geometry(), for a constructed lattice whose shared vertices do not coincide exactly.

Value

A logical matrix, symmetric, with a FALSE diagonal and both dimnames the codes at geoframe in member order.

Details

isolated is resolved after within has cut its edges, and the nearest feature is sought among those within allows. Fixing isolation first would hand a feature a neighbour that the mask then takes away again, leaving it isolated after all.

A feature whose within code is NA is its own group: unassigned codes do not silently pool.

On geographic (longitude/latitude) coordinates the two contiguity settings do not use the same engine: "queen" goes through sf::st_touches(), which is spherical under s2, while "rook" goes through sf::st_relate(), which has no spherical implementation and warns that it assumes the coordinates are planar. For contiguity the difference is immaterial – whether two polygons share a border does not depend on the metric – but project to an equal-area or local CRS first if the warning matters or the geometry crosses the antimeridian.

See also

geoscale_geometry(), geoscale_leaftable()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
a <- geoscale_adjacent(gs, geoframe = "region")
sum(a) / 2                                    # number of borders
geoscale_adjacent(gs, "region", within = "zone")        # confined
geoscale_adjacent(gs, "region", contiguity = "rook")    # edges only
} # }
